nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
﴿الم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾: there is consensus on the nominative of تنزيل, and its nominative is from three angles:
First, as mubtadaʾ (subject), with ﴿لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ as the khabar (predicate); second, by an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this which is recited is a revelation (tanzīl)"; and third, in the sense of "these letters are a revelation", «ألم» indicating all the letters just as أ ب ت ث indicate them. If تنزيل were accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) it would be permissible, just as the Kufans read ﴿إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 3–5].

nahhas-irab:3-4.t: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ﴾: «أم» indicates moving from one topic to another. ﴿بَلْ هُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); and likewise ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾. ﴿ما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾: i.e. the disbelievers have no protector who would prevent their punishment; ﴿وَلا شَفِيعٍ﴾: the nominative is also permissible, by [conjunction to] the position. ﴿أَفَلا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ this admonition.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾: Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read ﴿خَلْقَهُ﴾ with sukūn on the lām. Its accusative in this reading is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to Sībawayh, like ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Naml: 88]; according to others it is a badal (substitute) for «كلّ», i.e. "who perfected the creation of everything". On the school of some grammarians they are two objects, in the sense of "He made everything understand its creation". [The reading] ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾ takes it as a past verb in the position of the genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of شيء. The meaning, according to what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, is: He made firm everything He created, i.e. He brought it as He willed and it did not deviate from His will. Another view is that everything He creates is good, because no one is able to produce its like, and it points to its Creator. Abū Isḥāq said: الذي أحسن كلَّ شيءٍ خلقُه is also permissible with the nominative, in the sense "that is His creation". ﴿وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنْسانِ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾: meaning Adam ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ﴾: derived from سللت الشيء ("I drew the thing out"), and the pattern فُعالة is for a small quantity. ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ مَهِينٍ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. weak; and someone else said: i.e. of no worth among people.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ﴾: meaning the water. ﴿وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِهِ﴾: i.e. that by which he lives. ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ﴾: He made السمع singular and الأبصار plural, because السمع is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a singular indicating a plural. ﴿وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾: plural of فؤاد, which is the heart.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وقالوا أأذا ضللنا في الأرض أأنا لفي خلق جديد﴾, and it is also read ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾. In this there is a difficult question of Arabic grammar. It is asked: what governs «إذ» [Translator's note: so in the text; إذا is meant], when what follows «إنّ» does not govern what precedes it? And the question is harder with the interrogative, because what follows an interrogative is even more fitting not to govern what precedes it than [what follows] «أنّ»; so how [can it], when the two have come together? The answer, according to the reading of whoever read أنا [Translator's note: i.e. إِنَّا without the interrogative], is that the governor is ضللنا; and according to the reading of whoever read ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾, that the governor is implied (muḍmar), the implied meaning being "Shall we be resurrected when we have died?" There is also a question in it: it is asked, where is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا in the first reading, since it carries the sense of a condition? The answer to that is that it is followed by a past verb, and for that reason this is permissible. From Abū Rajāʾ and Ṭalḥa, that they read ﴿أَإِذا ضَلِلْنا﴾ [Translator's note: the distinctive vowelling (ضَلِلْنا, with kasra on the first lām) is not shown in the printed text], and it is an anomalous (shādhdh) dialect. And from al-Ḥasan: اإذا صللنا with ṣād; al-Farrāʾ related it thus, and claimed that it is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. صللنا is not known in the language, but صللنا is known [Translator's note: the vowel distinction between the two forms has been lost in the printed text; presumably صَلِلْنا is the unknown form and صَلَلْنا the known one]; one says صلّ اللحم وأصلّ, and خمّ وأخمّ, when [the meat] has gone rotten.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿قُلْ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: it is from paying a number in full (tawfiyat al-ʿadad), i.e. he takes your number in full, all of you.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ناكِسُوا رُؤُسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Abū Isḥāq said: the address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to his community, and the meaning is "If only you (plural) could see". The school of Abū al-ʿAbbās is otherwise: that the meaning is "O Muḥammad, say to the criminal: If you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, you would regret what you did"; the apodosis of «لو» and [the verb of] saying are omitted.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنا لَآتَيْنا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُداها﴾: two objects. It is said that there are two views on its meaning: one of them is that the context of the passage indicates that it concerns the Hereafter, i.e. if We willed, We would return them to the world and to the trial, as they asked. ﴿وَلكِنْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ مِنِّي لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾: i.e. the word from Me is due: I will surely punish whoever disobeys Me with the punishment of Hell; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knew that if He returned them they would go back, as He said: ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعادُوا لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 28]. [Translator's note: the second view is not stated in the text.]

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فَذُوقُوا بِما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا﴾: there are two views on its meaning: one is that it is from the forgetting that has no remembrance with it, i.e. you did not work for this day, so you were like those who forget; the other is that نسيتم means "you abandoned"; and likewise ﴿إِنَّا نَسِيناكُمْ﴾. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd adduced as proof His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنا إِلى آدَمَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 115]. He said: the proof that it means "abandoned" is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, related of Iblīs that he said to him: ﴿ما نَهاكُما رَبُّكُما عَنْ هذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 20]; so if Adam ﷺ had been forgetting, he [Iblīs] would have reminded him. And he recited [in the basīṭ metre]: 340-
كأنّه خارجا من جنب صفحته ... سفّود شرب نسوه عند مفتأد
(As though, jutting out from the side of its flank, it were the roasting-spit of a drinking party that they left behind at the fireplace.)
i.e. they left it; if it were from forgetting, they would have used it once.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّما يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنَا الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِّرُوا بِها خَرُّوا سُجَّداً﴾: i.e. only those believe in the signs, proofs and arguments who, when reminded of them, humble themselves before Allah and glorify Him with His praise. ﴿وَهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ from His worship nor from submitting to what He has made clear.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿تَتَجافى جُنُوبُهُمْ﴾: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or nominative because it is an imperfect verb; the inflection does not appear in it because it is a maqṣūr verb. The meaning of maqṣūr is that the inflection is withheld (quṣira) from it, and the meaning of manqūṣ is that the inflection is diminished (nuqiṣa) from it. ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿خَوْفاً﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿وَطَمَعاً﴾ is like it, i.e. out of fear of punishment and hope of reward. ﴿وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: «ما» may be in the sense of الذي ("that which") or a maṣdar; in both cases it must be written separately from «من».

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ﴾: it is also read ما أخفي لهم with sukūn on the yāʾ [i.e. أُخْفِيْ, "what I conceal"], as an imperfect verb. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ما نخفي ("what We conceal"), with nūn. Abū Isḥāq said: and it is read ما أخفي لهم [i.e. أَخْفى] in the sense of "what Allah has concealed for them". If you make «ما» in the sense of الذي ("that which"), it is in the position of the accusative on all the readings; and if you make it in the sense of أيّ ("which?") and read with the reading of the Medinans, it is in the position of the nominative, and if you read with another reading, it is in the position of the accusative.
﴿جَزاءً﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: [Translator's note: the entry opens without quoting the verse; it concerns ﴿أَفَمَنْ كانَ مُؤْمِناً كَمَنْ كانَ فاسِقاً لا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾.] Because the word «من» conveys a group, for this reason He said: لا يستوون ("they are not equal", plural). This is the view of many of the grammarians. Some of them said: يستوون is for two, except that two is a plural, because it is one gathered with another. The ḥadīth points to this view, because it is [reported] from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, and others, who said: ﴿أَفَمَنْ كانَ مُؤْمِناً﴾ was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and ﴿كَمَنْ كانَ فاسِقاً﴾ about al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: ﴿أَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described him with faith. The khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿فَلَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ الْمَأْوى﴾, and the meaning is: "for him and those like him"; on this basis the plural came. And likewise ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا فَمَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ﴾. ﴿كُلَّما﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ﴾: a lām of oath. ﴿مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْأَدْنى﴾: i.e. the nearer; most of the exegetes hold that it is the calamities in this world.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾: i.e. to himself. ﴿مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآياتِ رَبِّهِ﴾: i.e. with His proofs and signs. ﴿ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْها﴾ by refusing to accept; so know that He will take retribution on him. So He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّا مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ﴾: two objects. ﴿فَلا تَكُنْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقائِهِ﴾: we have already mentioned it. It has been said that its meaning is: "So be not in doubt about Moses ﷺ receiving the Book with acceptance." From al-Ḥasan, that he said regarding its meaning: "We certainly gave Moses the Book, and he was harmed and called a liar; so be not in doubt that what he met of denial and harm will meet you." This is an unusual view, besides being from the transmission of ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً﴾: the Kufans read أمّة [Translator's note: so in the printed text; from what follows the Kufan reading meant is أَأِمَّة, with two realised hamzas], and it is a solecism (laḥn) according to all the grammarians, because it combines two hamzas in a single word. This is one of the subtleties of grammar, and its explanation is that the original is أَأْمِمَة; then the vowel of the first mīm was cast onto the hamza, the mīm was assimilated into the mīm, and the second hamza was lightened so that two hamzas would not come together. Combining two hamzas in two words is far-fetched; as for in one word, it is not permissible at all, except with lightening, [as in] آدم and آخر; and this is of the same kind as آدم. ﴿لَمَّا صَبَرُوا﴾ [read as لِما صبروا means] "because of their patience"; and ﴿لَمَّا صَبَرُوا﴾ means: when they were patient, We made them leaders.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
﴿أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ﴾: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Qatāda read أو لمن نهد لهم [Translator's note: so in the printed text; أَوَلَمْ نَهْدِ لَهُمْ is meant] with nūn, and this is a clear reading. The first reading, with yāʾ, has a difficulty in it, because it is said: a verb is never without an agent, so where is the agent of يهد? The grammarians discussed this. Al-Farrāʾ said: «كم» is in the position of the nominative by يهد.
This contradicts the principles of the grammarians in their saying that an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it, nor is كم in any way, I mean by what precedes it. The school of Abū al-ʿAbbās is that يهد indicates guidance, so the meaning is "Has the guidance not guided them?" It has also been said that the meaning is "Has Allah not guided them?", so that the meaning of the yāʾ and the meaning of the nūn are the same. Abū Isḥāq said: كم is in the position of the accusative by أهلكنا. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ﴾: in the position of the accusative by إنّ. ﴿أَفَلا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ in the sense of "Will they not accept?", like سمع الله لمن حمده ("Allah hears (accepts) the one who praises Him").

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَسُوقُ الْماءَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ﴾: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it is the land of Yemen. Sufyān said: and Maʿmar related to me from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: it is Abyan. Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān said from ʿIkrima: «إلى الأرض الجرز»: he said:
it is the thirsty [land]. Juwaybir said from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ﴾: he said: the dead, parched [land]. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is the one in which there is no vegetation. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: الأرض الجرز is the one that grows nothing. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it is unlikely to be anything but a specific land, because of the entry of the alif and lām, except that it is permissible on the view of what Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said. Abū Jaʿfar said: the chain of transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās is sound, with no flaw in it; and this is only a naʿt (adjective), and the adjective of a definite noun is with the alif and lām. It is derived from their saying رجل جروز ("a voracious man"), when he leaves nothing without eating it. Al-Farrāʾ and others related that one says أرض جُرُز, جُرْز and جَرَز [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant forms is not given in the printed text; supplied here from the standard lexical sources], and likewise بخل, رعب and رهب: in the four there are four dialects. ﴿فَنُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعاً﴾: it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نسوق, or cut off from what precedes it. ﴿تَأْكُلُ مِنْهُ أَنْعامُهُمْ﴾: in the position of the accusative as a naʿt. ﴿وَأَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾: i.e. and they eat of it. In the speech of the Arabs النفس is of two kinds: one is that separateness is meant by it, and the other is that the whole of a thing and its reality is meant by it. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116], i.e. You know what I know and I do not know what You know. ﴿أَفَلا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾: (ألا) may be for drawing attention (tanbīh).

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْفَتْحُ﴾: «متى» is in the position of the nominative, and it may be in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). Al-Farrāʾ said: He means the conquest of Mecca. Better than this is what Mujāhid said; he said:
He means the Day of Resurrection. Abū Jaʿfar said: on the day of the conquest of Mecca, the faith of whoever believed did benefit him. It is related that the believers said: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will judge between us on the Day of Resurrection, and will reward the doer of good and punish the evildoer," so the disbelievers said mockingly: "When is this fatḥ?", i.e. this judgement. A judge is called فاتح and فتّاح because matters are opened up and decided at his hands; and in the Quran: ﴿رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 89].

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿قُلْ يَوْمَ الْفَتْحِ﴾: [accusative] as an adverb (ẓarf); al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾: it is said that its meaning is: turn away from their foolishness and do not answer them except with what you have been commanded.
﴿وَانْتَظِرْ إِنَّهُمْ مُنْتَظِرُونَ﴾: i.e. wait for the Day of the fatḥ, the day on which Allah will judge in your favour against them. If someone says: how can they be waiting for the Day of Resurrection when they do not believe in it? — there are two answers to this: one is that the meaning is that they are waiting for death, which is one of the causes of the Resurrection, so this would be figurative; and the other is that among them are some who doubt and some who are certain of the Resurrection, so this would be for these two kinds. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.
